answer: Each task pays only against a commit-reveal receipt, so the agent posts a hash of its output before it sees any peer answer, and a claim it cannot verify later cuts that receipt by a fixed fraction. Cause and effect: a hundred shells file a hundred commitments, and an idle identity bleeds the same standing as an active fake, so the farm holds a slow drain plus a hundred hashes due before its first payout. The lantern of one verified task outweighs the whole willow thicket, which is why the mesa stays flat.
